issues.description: The flattenRef invariant is not stated and now juggles three deletion regimes without a written contract
issues.detail: flattenRef now (a) merges ref schema, (b) restores child props, (c) deletes parent-only keys when isParentRef, (d) deletes keys equal to extracted $defs entries, and (e) optionally overrides $ref from parent. No comment states the postcondition (what `schema` is guaranteed to contain on exit). Without a literate invariant block, the next maintainer is operating on faith. NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT.

issues.description: Quadratic-with-stringify de-duplication on every flatten call
issues.detail: Two `for (key in schema)` loops call `JSON.stringify(schema[key]) === JSON.stringify(refSeen.def![key])` per key. For schemas with nested objects this is O(n*size) per node, and flattenRef recurses across the seen graph. ASYMPTOTICALLY-OK-PRACTICALLY-SLOW. A shallow structural compare or a `===` fast-path before stringify would remove the worst constants; at minimum, document why stringify is acceptable here.

issues.description: overrideCount jumped 6 to 12 with no explanation of why doubling is correct
issues.detail: The test assertion changed from 6 to 12 — a 2x increase in override callbacks. The PR rationale (removing `if (!seen.isParent)` guard) explains the mechanism but not the semantic contract: are users now expected to receive override calls for parent/wrapper schemas they previously did not see? This is a behavior change for any consumer using `override`. State the new invariant: override fires exactly once per seen entry.

issues.description: Termination of mutually recursive flattenRef calls rests on a single sentinel with no proof
issues.detail: flattenRef recurses into `seen.ref` then later into `seen.parent`, guarded only by `seen.ref === null`. But `seen.parent` has no such sentinel — re-entering through the parent branch could re-trigger work if a node is reached via two paths. Termination is plausible but unproved. Add a comment stating the termination argument, or introduce a `seen.flattened` boolean.

issues.description: Separating `ref` (processor-set) from `parent` (clone-chain) is the right data structure move but is undocumented
issues.detail: The new `Seen.parent` field is the correct data-structure decision — conflating the two was the original bug. However the JSDoc is one line each and does not explain the relationship: when can they differ, when must they agree, who is responsible for setting each. A small literate block above the `Seen` interface would prevent the next regression.

issues.description: play.ts committed with local-path import and exploratory console.log code
issues.detail: play.ts now imports from `./packages/zod/src/index.js` (a developer's local scratch path) and contains exploratory `console.log` calls. This is fine as a scratchpad but should not land in the PR — it is the kind of artifact that survives because nobody re-reads diffs. Revert or move to a gitignored scratch file.

review.summary: The fix correctly identifies that conflating processor-`ref` with clone-chain-`parent` was the root cause, and splitting them in the `Seen` structure is the right data-structure move — Knuth would approve of the diagnosis. However the implementation is UNDER-AUDITED: flattenRef now carries five distinct responsibilities without a stated loop/recursion invariant, the de-duplication uses JSON.stringify in an inner loop (ASYMPTOTICALLY-OK-PRACTICALLY-SLOW), and the override-count doubling (6 to 12) is a behavior change with no documented contract. None of this is wrong, but the literate-programming layer that would let the next maintainer verify correctness without running the code is missing. Tighten the comments, fast-path the equality check, and ship.
